text:
Priya: heads up — CI flagged an attestation regression for the new minimal base image. cosign verification failing during canary deploy :frowning:
Ryan: saw that earlier, looks like the KMS signer principal lost iam:Sign after last week's RBAC prune.
Sam: oh — which principal? the cosign-service account in prod-kms?
Priya: yes, service-account/cosign-signer@redwood-prod. The error is `rpc error: code = PermissionDenied desc = signing denied` from kms.
Maya: devsec-bot just posted the scan: \n\n```
devsec-bot: IMAGE_SCAN: base-minimal:sha256:abc123 - ATTACHMENT_FAILED - attestation.verify - cosign: verification error: rpc signing denied
```
Jordan: that matches. I removed a couple of broad roles during the RBAC cleanup — may have accidentally removed kms.signer grant for that SA.
Ryan: quick mitigation: we can add a short-lived fallback that uses a dedicated ephemeral signer in staging to keep canary alive while we fix prod.
Priya: agree, but we need to be explicit about audit logging. If we re-grant iam:Sign to the service account, we must ensure the key usage goes to auditing S3/bigquery with 90d retention and alert on cross-region usage.
Sam: who owns the key policy? is it under infra-kms/redwood-signers? I can open a request with ops if you confirm the exact key resource name.
Maya: key is projects/redwood-prod/locations/global/keyRings/signer/cryptoKeys/cosign-key
Jordan: +1 to Sam opening a ticket. Also let's update the RBAC change log entry and include a link to the audit export. We don't want this flip-flop repeating.
Priya: action list: 1) Sam open ops ticket to re-grant Sign on cosign-signer SA for that key (with conditional: source IP = infra CIDR and bound to cosign workflow) 2) Ryan create ephemeral-staging-signer and route canary attestations to it 3) Jordan update RBAC PR to add a unit test that fails if signer loses permission 4) Maya ensure audit export path and retention are set
Sam: filing ticket now: OPS-4721 — requesting iam.roles/cryptoSign for service-account/cosign-signer@redwood-prod on cosign-key. tagging @OpsOnCall and @Priya for approvals.
OpsOnCall: got it, reviewing. FYI — any permission change will trigger a key rotation if we rebind principals, we should coordinate a short maintenance window.
Ryan: for the ephemeral workaround, I'll push a helm patch to route canary images with label `attestation=ephemeral` to staging signer. Patch will be small and revertable.
Priya: good. Also we discovered a vuln in one of the base packages (CVE-2026-9999) flagged by the scan — not exploitable in our runtime but needs tracking in vuln triage board. Jordan please open an issue and tag Product Security.
Jordan: created SEC-2902: CVE-2026-9999 - base-minimal - triage needed. Assigned to Maya for impact assessment.
Maya: I'll run the binary diff between old and new base images and list any setuid bits and suspicious libs. ETA 3h.
Sam: once Maya confirms low impact we can proceed with signer restore and canary. If not, we pause and rebuild base image without the offending package.
Priya: don't forget to update the runtime mitigations doc — seccomp profile + userns mapping should be tightened if we rebuild.
Ryan: noted. I'll also add a temporary runtime config that disables privileged mounts for canary pods.
devsec-bot: NOTE: DEPLOYMENT_HOLD detected for canary/base-minimal - awaiting attestation verification.
OpsOnCall: if the fix requires key rotation, schedule it for 02:00 UTC to minimize customer impact. I'll set the tentative window.
Priya: summary: Sam files ops ticket (done), Ops reviews (on it), Ryan implements ephemeral signer patch (working), Maya does vuln impact (3h), Jordan files triage issue (done). We'll reconvene in this thread after Ops responds. Thanks :thumbsup:
Ryan: quick Q — do we want to add a CI gate that verifies KMS permissions for the cosign principal on every RBAC change? Might reduce surprises.
Jordan: yes, we can add a terraform plan check that queries IAM bindings and fails PRs removing `roles/cloudkms.signerVerifier` from known signers. I'll prototype.
Priya: perfect. Also update runbook 'attestation-failure' with the new rollback steps (route to ephemeral signer, pause canary, re-grant permissions). I'll make a PR after Ops approves the permission change.
Sam: ops responded: "we'll apply the permission during the 02:00 UTC window; no rotation required as long as binding is additive." Adding OpsOnCall and Priya to the change request now.
Maya: confirmed minimal impact on vuln so far, no setuid changes. safe to proceed with signer restore post-window.
Jordan: cool, marking SEC-2902 -> triaged-low for now.
Priya: thanks everyone. I'll bump the runbook and close the loop after the 02:00 change. If anything blocks, ping OpsOnCall and re-open this thread.
Ryan: will monitor the canary after the fix and report attestation status here.
devsec-bot: ATTACHMENT_STATUS: base-minimal canary - pending -> will re-run post-change\n
